entries.subject: Bulge
entries.finding: Salo et al. (2015), S4G Pipeline 4, table 7, NGC4826, model _bdd: a Sérsic bulge (28.0% of the light, magnitude 9.229, half-light radius 28.96″ = 0.61 kpc, n = 4.164, axis ratio 0.699, PA 102.38°) and an exponential disc (67.9% of the light, scale length 56.23″ = 1.19 kpc, axis ratio 0.554, PA 115.88°, face-on central surface brightness 19.018, 18.377 as projected on the sky) and an exponential disc (4.2% of the light, scale length 17.38″ = 0.37 kpc, axis ratio 0.554, PA 115.88°, face-on central surface brightness 19.486, 18.845 as projected on the sky). Used as published; the half-light surface brightness the bake needs, 19.559 mag per square arcsecond, follows from the bulge's magnitude, radius, index and axis ratio. At the disc's 59.1° the bulge's axis ratio is one an oblate spheroid in the disc plane can show (intrinsic 0.55).
